/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/tip.source_en: **FREE observatory hack**: book N Grill or HanCook in advance. Otherwise, the panoramic concourse views at the base are mostly FREE. Visit at sunset for the day-to-night transition (queue at 17:00 for 18:00 sunset in summer). Cable car queues hit 20+ min on weekends — plan accordingly. NEVER take a taxi — taxis are prohibited from the park.

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: N Grill revolving restaurant (free observatory with reservation), HanCook (free observatory with reservation), Cinnabon, A Twosome Place, multiple cafes, Game Plaza arcade.

/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: N Seoul Tower is Seoul's #1 'photo this means I was in Korea' landmark — and the 360° view orientates first-time visitors to Seoul's geography (Bukhansan north, Han River south, Gangnam east). Picked over Lotte World Tower (taller at 555 m / world's 5th tallest) because Namsan's central location AND lower elevation actually deliver better intermediate-distance views of the historic central districts (Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon) that you've just visited. The 360° view also delivers a **memorable photo album anchor** — the 'Locks of Love' wall + N Seoul Tower exterior + the Seoul cityscape make this the day's most-shared social-media moment for first-time cruise visitors.

/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en:
⟦G0⟧ is Seoul's most iconic landmark — a 236.7-meter broadcasting and observation tower atop Namsan Mountain (243 m), with the tower's apex 479.7 m above sea level. Originally constructed 1969-1971 as Korea's first comprehensive broadcasting tower (TV/radio multi-broadcaster), it opened to the public 1980 and was rebranded 'N Seoul Tower' in December 2005 after CJ Foodville renovated the observation levels. 

Recognized by foreign tourists in a 2012 Seoul Metropolitan Government survey as Korea's #1 tourist attraction, and selected with Changdeokgung as one of Lonely Planet's Ultimate Travel List Top 500 destinations (2015) — approximately 12 million annual visitors. 

The signature visitor experiences: **the 360° observation deck** (Adult 21,000 KRW / Senior+Child 16,000 KRW; weekdays 10:30-22:00, weekends 10:00-23:00 — last admission 30 min before close); the iconic **Locks of Love wall** on the terrace where couples attach padlocks; the revolving **N Grill restaurant** (one rotation per ~48 min for a panoramic dining experience — diners with advance reservation get FREE observatory access); and **Korea's first aerial tramway** the **Namsan Cable Car** (opened 1962, predates the tower by 9 years, 605 m route, ~3 min ride, max altitude 138 m). 

K-drama filming legacy includes 'My Love From The Star,' 'Boys Over Flowers,' 'Korean Odyssey (Hwayugi).' **Critical note**: TAXIS ARE PROHIBITED from entering the park (environmental protection) — your private vehicle drops at the Namsan Cable Car base or Namsan Yejang parking, and you ride the cable car or walk the final ~10 min.
